column1: # CIRIS evidence registry — the `state:blocked-upstream` adoption manifest.
# Each row is an upstream obligation the client's build contract waits on,
# expressed as a SCANNABLE PREDICATE: a needle whose appearance in the named
# kind: absence | drift | untestable  (see the CIRISServer registry)

column9: The node does not serve its own OpenAPI spec. The client carries a committed copy and is graded against it, which means the contract is owned by the party under test. The three current "OpenAPI" mentions in src are prose comments. readiness spec-drift can only ask its question once a route serves the document.

generated-api is ~730 committed files produced by openapi-generator (config in openapi-generator-config.yaml) and nothing re-runs the generator, so spec drift is silent. A generator task in the build graph is the fix; readiness generated-api-drift stays unimplemented until then.
The lane these gates are the pre-flight for (#86 §2). Until it exists, a client regression cannot block a CIRISServer or CIRISAgent release.
The client test band. Bands 0xx/1xx/2xx/3xx/5xx/9xx are in use; 6xx is free and unclaimed.

CC 3.1.2.1 pins the locale-manifest leaf domain as ciris.locale_manifest.v2 with a field named locale; the shipped floor carries v1 and lang_code (documented in CIRISConformance test_578_locale_provenance). Until that closes, the client locale bundle cannot be checked against a signed Merkle root and the four-bundle byte-identity guard stands in for it. CIRISVerify is not in this repo reachable tree, so there is nothing local to scan. NO UPSTREAM ISSUE NUMBER IS KNOWN — one needs filing; this row is the obligation, not the tracker.
